Subject: Region pinning proof + deletion test window

Hi Chloe,

We reviewed the dedicated deployment brief and have a couple of asks before we can sign off on the PO. HelioBank requires:

1) A documented test plan that proves tenant data remains within EU-bound PVCs when region pinning is enabled (no cross-region fallback during node maintenance).
2) Evidence of a tenant-scoped deletion (wipe) including a time-to-complete for live data + snapshots, and the list of logs/archives retained post-wipe.
3) A short list of what you can provide as audit artifacts for our internal auditors (hashes, wipe receipts, snapshot tombstones).

Can you share a plan and a target testing window next week? We prefer a non-business-hour window CET.

Thanks,
Marta K.
SecOps, HelioBank

Hi Marta — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, longer plan below.

- Yes — we can run an isolated validation (non-production tenant) with region pinning enforced and show observability that no egress occurred to non-EU AZs during maintenance.
- Wipe path: live object deletion + snapshot tombstone + metadata purge; typical completion for medium-tenancy (up to 5TB) during a full wipe is ~2–4 hours end-to-end in active clusters; snapshot tombstones appear within 15 minutes after job completion and background garbage collection completes within 24 hours (we'll provide timestamps).
- Audit artifacts we can provide: wipe job run-id, UUIDs for affected storage objects, incremental checksums before/after, KMS key usage logs, and a signed receipt (HMAC) from the dedicated control plane.

Attached is a draft test plan (geo-lock-test-plan.pdf) and a sample wipe evidence extract (wipe-evidence-sample.txt). Please review and tell us which CET evening works for you. Proposed window: 2026-09-10 20:00–23:00 CET.

I'll loop Aditya and Karthik for the low-level details below.

Best,
Chloe Martin
Enterprise Success — Redwood Inference

Marta / Chloe — technical addendum on how we prove locality: 

1) During the test we run a read/write workload that stamps objects with tenant-specific identifiers plus a unique test nonce. Network egress is observed from the host-level routing table and from our internal telemetry — both must show EU-only routes.
2) For maintenance simulation we will trigger a controlled node drain on the primary EU AZ and observe that the autoscaler either re-allocates workload to EU spare capacity or fails indication (no cross-region promotion). We will capture allocation events, node-to-tenant mapping, and routing table snapshots.
3) Wipe details: tiered deletion stages (live object delete -> snapshot tombstone -> GC sweep). Snapshots are immutable; creating a tombstone marks them for GC. We will provide the tombstone timestamp and subsequent GC completion event.

Note: If HelioBank requires physical-host attestation (hypervisor-level evidence), we can provide cluster export of host IDs and allocation logs — but that is on a per-contract basis. For the standard Dedicated SOW we include the artifacts listed by Chloe.

- Aditya (Sr. Infra Engineer)

Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 09:05:00 -0700

Hi all — adding retention/backup clarifications so auditors get a clean mapping:

- Customer primary objects (S3 interface) are removed immediately at the time of a tenant wipe; object tombstones are recorded with a wipe run id.
- Automated hourly snapshots (if enabled) are retained per the tenant snapshot policy; when a wipe is invoked we also create a forced snapshot tombstone and schedule GC in the same job.
- Backup replicas: for Dedicated with geo-pin we prevent cross-region replication; backups remain in-region.
- Logs: control-plane audit logs (request traces, KMS unwrap events) are retained for 365 days by default for Enterprise customers; object-level activity logs we can export as CSV for the test period.

I'll prepare a snapshot retention matrix (attached) showing TTLs and when GC markers are emitted.

Karthik
Senior Product Manager — Redwood Inference

Thanks — quick follow-ups from our side:

- Can you confirm whether the signed receipt is stored outside the tenant storage (we need an independent artifact)?
- For snapshot tombstones: can you include the tombstone object names/IDs in the artefacts so our auditors can map them to what they see in the cluster export?
- We also want to see a simulated forced-wipe run where the tenant's KMS key is rotated post-wipe to show crypto-material unlinking (no key access means prior ciphertext cannot be recovered). Is key rotation part of your standard wipe flow or an extra step?

If all that is doable we can proceed with the proposed window.

Marta

From: chloe.martin@redwood.com

Hi Marta — short answers:

- Signed receipt: stored in our control plane's immutable audit bucket (separate tenant), and we can additionally provide a signed PDF/matching HMAC over the wipe job output as an independent artifact.
- Tombstone IDs: yes, we'll include the list of tombstone object IDs as part of the wipe evidence bundle.
- KMS rotation: not automatic as part of the default wipe (we keep key lifecycle separate) but we will run a rotation in the test as an additional step and capture the KMS rotation event and resulting unwrap failures against archived ciphertexts. We will treat that rotation as an opt-in test action and include it in the runbook.

I've updated the test plan to include the KMS rotation step and an independent signed receipt export. If HelioBank confirms the window we'll schedule the dry run on 2026-09-10 20:00–22:00 CET and a recorded production-level run on 2026-09-11 02:00–05:00 CET (if you want both nights).

Regards,
Chloe
